report.answer_text:
TikTok briefly went dark in the U.S. in January 2025, then stayed online while ByteDance negotiated a deal to restructure its U.S. operations. The deal was signed in December 2025, but it didn’t close until January 22, 2026. (tradingview.com)
January: On January 17, the Supreme Court upheld a 2024 law requiring ByteDance, TikTok’s China-based parent, to divest its U.S. operations or face a ban. TikTok shut off U.S. access late on January 18 and began restoring it on January 19 after President-elect Donald Trump promised to delay enforcement. Apple and Google didn’t restore the app to their U.S. stores until February 13. (supremecourt.gov)
January through September: Trump repeatedly delayed enforcement while negotiations continued. On September 25, he signed an executive order approving the proposed ownership framework and giving the parties more time to complete the deal. (whitehouse.gov)
December: On December 18, TikTok and ByteDance signed binding agreements to form a majority American-owned joint venture. Oracle, Silver Lake, and Abu Dhabi-based MGX would each hold 15%, while ByteDance would retain 19.9%. The venture would oversee U.S. user data, recommendation-algorithm security, and content moderation. The deal covered TikTok’s U.S. operations, not the sale of TikTok globally. (ksl.com)

quotes.text: January 18, 2025 - TikTok stops working for users in the United States late on Saturday, disappears from Apple and Google app stores before the law shutting it down on national security grounds took effect on Sunday.

pages.quote_reason: The quote states that TikTok stopped working for U.S. users on January 18, 2025, which backs the claim that it briefly went dark in the U.S. in January 2025 (the word 'briefly' is not explicitly stated but the quote's wording about stopping and being removed from app stores before the law took effect is consistent with a temporary outage).
pages.page_reason: The page states that on January 18, 2025, TikTok stopped working for users in the United States and disappeared from app stores, and service was restored on January 19, 2025, which directly supports the claim that it briefly went dark in the U.S. in January 2025.

claims.sentence: TikTok briefly went dark in the U.S. in January 2025, then stayed online while ByteDance negotiated a deal to restructure its U.S. operations.

quotes.text: January 18, 2025 - TikTok stops working for users in the United States late on Saturday, disappears from Apple and Google app stores before the law shutting it down on national security grounds took effect on Sunday.

January 19, 2025 - TikTok says it is restoring service after then President-elect Donald Trump said he would revive the app's access in the U.S. when he returns to power on Monday. Deadline extended to early April.

pages.quote_reason: The quotes back the brief blackout in January 2025 and the restoration of service, but they never mention ByteDance negotiating a deal or restructuring U.S. operations, and only say the deadline was extended to early April.
pages.page_reason: The page says TikTok went dark on January 18, 2025, was restored on January 19 after Trump's intervention, and then had its sale deadline repeatedly extended while White House-led talks on a U.S. ownership deal continued, with a framework reached in September 2025 to keep it operating.

claims.sentence: The deal was signed in December 2025, but it didn’t close until January 22, 2026. (tradingview.com)
claims.claim: The ByteDance deal to restructure TikTok's U.S. operations was signed in December 2025.

quotes.text: September 15, 2025 - U.S. and Chinese officials reach a framework agreement to switch TikTok to U.S.-controlled ownership that will be confirmed in a Friday call between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.
September 16, 2025 - Trump says the U.S. and China have a deal that will keep TikTok operating and that the U.S. will announce a buyer.

pages.quote_reason: The quotes date the framework agreement and Trump's announcement to September 2025 and describe a deal still pending confirmation, with nothing indicating it was signed in December 2025, so the claim's date is not backed and the quoted timeline points to September instead.
pages.page_reason: The page says Trump announced a deal on September 16, 2025 and that the deadline was extended to December 16, but it does not state that any deal was signed in December 2025, so the claim is not supported.

claims.sentence: The deal was signed in December 2025, but it didn’t close until January 22, 2026. (tradingview.com)

quotes.text: Accordingly, I have determined that the proposed divestiture would allow the millions of Americans who enjoy TikTok every day to continue using it while also protecting national security.

Based on these findings, I further determine that the divestiture of the applications outlined in the Framework Agreement, once its implementation agreements are executed, is a “qualified divestiture” under the Act

pages.page_reason: The page is Executive Order 14352 dated September 25, 2025, which determines the Framework Agreement's divestiture is a qualified divestiture, and it is signed by Donald J. Trump, so the claim that he signed an order approving the proposed TikTok framework on September 25 is supported.

quotes.text: To permit the contemplated divestiture to be completed, the Attorney General shall not take any action on behalf of the United States to enforce the Act for 120 days from the date of this order.

pages.page_reason: The page says the September 25 order directs the Attorney General not to enforce the Act for 120 days 'to permit the contemplated divestiture to be completed,' which effectively gives more time to finish the deal, though the order itself is issued by the President rather than the parties.

quotes.text: WASHINGTON — TikTok's Chinese owner, ByteDance, signed binding agreements with three major investors to sell just over 80% of the company's U.S. assets to American and global investors to avoid a government ban, TikTok CEO Shou Zi Chew told employees on Thursday.

The details of the deal are in line with one unveiled in September, when Trump delayed until Jan. 20 enforcement of the law that bans the app unless its Chinese owners sell it amid efforts to extract TikTok's U.S. assets from the global platform.

pages.quote_reason: The quotes state the deal involved selling just over 80% of TikTok's U.S. assets and extracting those U.S. assets from the global platform, which together back the claim that the deal covered U.S. operations rather than a global sale.
pages.page_reason: The page says ByteDance agreed to sell just over 80% of TikTok's U.S. assets and that the deal aims to extract U.S. assets from the global platform, which supports that it concerned U.S. operations rather than a global sale, though it does not explicitly state that global operations were excluded.
